extracted.intended_audience: citizens, delegates, and political thinkers drafting or evaluating constitutions (founding-era American audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and legal provisions for designing, evaluating, and operating a constitutionally ordered government, including political-theory cautions and the text of a written constitution (Preamble, Articles I–II). Useful for framers, lawmakers, and constitutional commentators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of executive from legislative; bicameral correction
rubrics_metrics.description: “The best way that can be conceived of, surely, is to separate the executive power from the legislative, make it responsible to one part of the legislature, on the impeachment of another, for the exercise of its power of appointment to offices, and to appoint two assemblies in the legislature, that the errors of one may be corrected by the other.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design government so the executive is distinct from the legislature; make the executive accountable to one legislative chamber while another can impeach; use two legislative assemblies (bicameralism) so each checks the other's errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent false charges while preserving accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid false charges, accusations, and calumnations against persons in authority while keeping magistrates and public officers accountable and liable to render an account of their behaviour and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance freedom to accuse with safeguards (independent grand jury, judicious adjudication by a senate or similar body, penalties for calumniators such as Roman Turpitianum) so that accountability does not become partisan persecution; recognize that simple democracies may struggle to maintain this balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit continuations and accessions of power; guard against honor-induced corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware of ingratitude and of placing trust in hands further than may be recalled at pleasure; 'honores mutant mores' — accessions and continuations of power expose the mind to temptations and high thoughts, producing ambition and danger to public freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid long, unchecked continuations of office or indefinite accumulation of honors and emoluments; design recall/term limits and structural checks to reduce temptations of ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentration of authority in a single representative assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: A government where the whole authority is in one representative assembly gives latitude, temptation, and opportunity to private ambition and corruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer mixed or tripartite compositions (separate branches, bicameral legislature, an independent executive) to reduce the risk of ambition and usurpation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and punish treason as crime against the people’s interest and majesty
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be made an unpardonable crime to incur the guilt of treason against the interest and majesty of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat conspiracies to subvert or betray the public interest as the gravest of crimes and provide strict penalties; note practical enforcement difficulties in simple democracies where conspirators may control instruments of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against foreign influence and bribery of public officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid private conferences with foreign ambassadors; receiving gifts or pensions from foreign princes or states is corrupting and may be treated as treasonable or severely punishable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict acceptance of foreign emoluments and private dealings with foreign agents; keep the executive/ministerial layer small and accountable to reduce avenues for foreign purchase of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative power vested in Congress (bicameral)
rubrics_metrics.description: “All legislative powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States, which shall consist of a Senate and House of Representatives.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitute a national legislature composed of two houses to exercise the legislative powers granted by the constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: House of Representatives: composition, qualifications, and apportionment
rubrics_metrics.description: The House shall be composed of members chosen every second year by the people; no person shall be a Representative who is under 25 years of age, nor not seven years a citizen, nor, when elected, an inhabitant of that state. Representatives and direct taxes shall be apportioned among the several states according to their respective numbers, including three-fifths of 'other persons' (3/5ths clause).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set age, citizenship, and residency qualifications; require periodic elections; provide for enumeration (census) and apportionment rules (historical 3/5ths rule appears here).

rubrics_metrics.name: House sole power of impeachment
rubrics_metrics.description: The House of Representatives shall have the sole power of impeachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign initial impeachment authority to the lower chamber, reserving trial and conviction to another body (the Senate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate: composition, qualifications, and impeachment trial role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senate shall be composed of two senators from each state, chosen by the legislature thereof, for six years; no person shall be a Senator who is under 30 years of age and not nine years a citizen. The Senate shall have the sole power to try all impeachments; conviction requires concurrence of two-thirds of members present; when the President is tried, the Chief Justice shall preside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide longer terms, equal state representation, higher age/citizenship requirements, and give the upper chamber responsibility for trying impeachments with a two-thirds conviction threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Times, places, and manner of elections; congressional assembly schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Times, places, and manner of holding elections for Senators and Representatives shall be prescribed in each state by the legislature thereof, but Congress may at any time by law make or alter such regulations, except as to the places of choosing Senators. Congress shall assemble at least once every year (first Monday in December unless law appoints different day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow state regulation of elections with federal override power (subject to exception); require regular sessions of the national legislature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each House judges its members; quorum, rules, journals, and expulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: Each house shall be the judge of the elections, returns, and qualifications of its own members; a majority constitutes a quorum; each house may determine rules, punish members for disorderly behavior, expel with two-thirds concurrence; keep a journal of proceedings with Yeas and Nays entered at request of one-fifth of those present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant internal self-governance, discipline, and transparency obligations to each chamber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and speech/debate privilege; immunity from arrest during attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Senators and Representatives shall receive compensation as ascertained by law, paid from the Treasury. They shall be privileged from arrest during attendance at sessions and in going to and returning from the same (except for treason, felony, and breach of the peace), and for any speech or debate in either house they shall not be questioned in any other place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect legislators' independence and freedom of debate, subject to narrow criminal exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility/clause against self-dealing appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: No Senator or Representative, during the time for which he was elected, shall be appointed to any civil office created, or the emoluments of which shall have been increased, during such time; and no person holding any office under the United States shall be a member of either house during his continuance in office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent legislators from creating or increasing offices/emoluments for their own later appointment; bar officeholders from simultaneous legislative membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue bills originate in the House; presentment and veto procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: All bills for raising revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives; every bill passed by both houses shall be presented to the President for approval; if disapproved he shall return it with objections, and if two-thirds of that house agree it shall be sent to the other house; a two-thirds vote of both houses can repass. If not returned in ten days (Sundays excepted) it becomes law unless Congress by adjournment prevents its return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign origination of revenue measures to the people’s chamber; provide a presentment clause including presidential veto and legislative override rules and the pocket veto consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated congressional powers (general list and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress shall have power: to lay and collect taxes, duties, imposts and excises; to borrow money; to regulate commerce with foreign nations, among the states, and with Indian tribes; to establish uniform rules of naturalization and uniform bankruptcy laws; to coin money and fix standards of weights and measures; to punish counterfeiting; to establish post offices and post roads; to promote the progress of science and useful arts by securing exclusive rights to authors and inventors (IP clause); to constitute inferior tribunals; to define and punish piracy and felonies on the high seas and offences against the law of nations; to declare war and make rules concerning captures; to raise and support armies (but appropriations not for longer than two years); to provide and maintain a navy; to make rules for government of land and naval forces; to call forth the militia to execute laws, suppress insurrections, and repel invasions; to organize, arm, and discipline the militia (reserving appointment of officers to states); to exercise exclusive legislation over the federal district and federal properties; and to make all laws necessary and proper for executing the foregoing powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerate specific national powers while including a Necessary and Proper clause to permit execution of those powers; include fiscal, military, commerce, IP, judicial, and administrative authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slave trade/migration/importation limitation (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: The migration or importation of such persons as any of the states shall think proper to admit shall not be prohibited by Congress prior to the year 1808, but a tax or duty may be imposed on such importation, not exceeding ten dollars for each person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical transitional limitation on Congress's ability to prohibit the importation of persons (note: contextual/historical clause addressed in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of habeas corpus only in rebellion or invasion
rubrics_metrics.description: The privilege of the writ of habeas corpus shall not be suspended, unless when in cases of rebellion or invasion the public safety may require it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect individual liberty by default; permit suspension only under severe public-safety emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on bills of attainder and ex post facto laws
rubrics_metrics.description: No bill of attainder or ex post facto law shall be passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbid legislative acts that punish specific persons or retroactively criminalize conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct taxes and apportionment rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No capitation, or other direct, tax shall be laid, unless in proportion to the census or enumeration herein directed to be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require apportionment of direct taxes according to population counts (census).

rubrics_metrics.name: No export duties; no preferential port treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: No tax or duty shall be laid on articles exported from any state; no preference shall be given by any regulation of commerce or revenue to the ports of one state over those of another; vessels bound to or from one state shall not be obliged to enter, clear, or pay duties in another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent interstate economic favoritism and export taxation that discriminates among states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations and financial transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: No money shall be drawn from the Treasury but in consequence of appropriations made by law; a regular statement and account of the receipts and expenditures of all public money shall be published from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require legislative appropriations for expenditures and periodic public accounting and transparency of public finances.

rubrics_metrics.name: No titles of nobility; restriction on accepting foreign emoluments
rubrics_metrics.description: No title of nobility shall be granted by the United States; and no person holding any office of profit or trust under them shall, without the consent of Congress, accept of any present, emolument, office, or title, of any kind whatever, from any king, prince, or foreign state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit a nobility system and restrict foreign gifts/emoluments to officeholders unless Congress consents, to prevent foreign influence and favoritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: State prohibitions on certain acts (Article I, Sec. 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: No state shall enter into any treaty, alliance, or confederation; grant letters of marque and reprisal; coin money; emit bills of credit; make anything but gold and silver coin a tender in payment of debts; pass any bill of attainder, ex post facto law, or law impairing the obligation of contracts; or grant any title of nobility. No state shall, without the consent of Congress, lay any imposts or duties on imports or exports (except as necessary for inspection laws), nor lay any duty of tonnage, keep troops or ships of war in time of peace, enter into any agreement or compact with another state or foreign power, or engage in war unless actually invaded or in imminent danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit states' abilities to conduct foreign policy, currency issuance, create special legal punishments, impair contracts, or otherwise conflict with national uniformity; reserve those competences to the national government or require federal consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive power vested in the President; term and election method
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive power shall be vested in a President of the United States of America. He shall hold his office during the term of four years, and, together with the Vice-President, chosen for the same term, be elected as follows: each state shall appoint, in such manner as the legislature thereof may direct, a number of electors equal to the whole number of Senators and Representatives to which the state may be entitled; no Senator or Representative, or person holding an office of trust or profit under the United States, shall be appointed an elector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vest executive authority in a single President with a fixed term; use an electoral college system with state-appointed electors, excluding certain federal officeholders from appointment as electors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impeachment judgment limits and criminal liability after conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgment in cases of impeachment shall not extend further than removal from office and disqualification to hold and enjoy any office of honor, trust, or profit under the United States; but the party convicted shall nevertheless be liable and subject to indictment, trial, judgment, and punishment, according to law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify that impeachment penalties are removal and disqualification, but do not preclude subsequent criminal prosecution in ordinary courts.
